sights.name: Portsmouth Historic Dockyard
sights.price: £36 for a 1-day 1-attraction ticket, £51 for all attractions for 1-year
sights.content: A major naval heritage site within an active Royal Navy base, featuring historic warships including ''HMS Victory'' and ''HMS Warrior''. It also includes the National Museum of the Royal Navy and other museums, exhibitions and interactive a

sights.name: Mary Rose Museum
sights.price: £36 for a 1-day ticket, £51 for all dockyard attractions for 1-year
sights.content: The Mary Rose Museum houses the remains of Henry VIII’s flagship, which sank in 1545 and was raised in 1982 after more than 400 years underwater. The museum is built around the preserved hull, displayed in a climate-controlled environment a

sights.name: Spinnaker Tower
sights.content: This striking and highly visible £21-million landmark tower rises some 170 m above the redeveloping harbour of Portsmouth, symbolising the wind filling a spinnaker sail. Visitors can use the tower to view from 3 levels: at 100 m, 105 m and

sights.name: Southsea Castle
sights.content: Built in 1544, the castle was part of a series of fortifications constructed by Henry VIII around England's coasts to protect the country from invaders. Heavily modified due to being in use until the end of World War II. Contains a rather r

sights.name: Southsea Model Village
sights.content: A 1/12 scale village

sights.name: Southsea Rose Garden
sights.content: Inside the 19th-century Lumps Fort.

sights.name: Ernest Smith Clock Tower
sights.content: A beautiful clock tower over a barbers.

sights.name: Portsmouth Cathedral
sights.content: A Romanesque Anglican cathedral in the old town. Contains a piece of Lord Nelson's flag and the tomb of a unknown member of the crew of the Mary Rose.

sights.name: St John's Catholic Cathedral
sights.content: A Catholic cathedral in the city centre.

sights.name: Royal Garrison Church
sights.content: A partly roofless English Heritage property. Only occasionally open to the public.

sights.name: Royal Marines Museum
sights.content: Covers the history of the Royal Marines. The museum is in what was one of the most stately Officers' Messes in England, built in the 1860s with beautiful ceilings, huge paintings and a grand staircase.

sights.name: Eastney Beam Engine House
sights.hours: open one day a month, check before visiting
sights.content: Pair of compound beam engines built in 1887 to pump sewage.

sights.name: The D-Day Story
sights.content: Tells the story of Operation Overlord during the Normandy D-Day landings including the Overlord Embroidery. Has an original LCT (landing craft tank) used at D-Day that has been restored and accessed by visitors.

sights.name: Blue Reef Aquarium
sights.content: Take an undersea safari at the aquarium on the seafront.

sights.name: Charles Dickens Birthplace Museum
sights.content: The famous writer Charles Dickens was born in this modest house in 1812.

sights.name: Cumberland House Natural History Museum
sights.content: A fairly limited collection.

sights.name: Portsmouth Museum and Art Gallery
sights.content: The Arthur Conan Doyle and Sherlock Holmes exhibition "A Study in Sherlock" is temporarily closed.

sights.name: Portsdown Hill
sights.content: Offers amazing views across Portsmouth and the South Downs. Just to the rear (north) of Portsmouth, it is a world away with countryside walks and traditional pubs.

sights.name: The Royal Armouries at Fort Nelson
sights.content: Sits just on Portsdown Hill and is free of charge to visit.

foodDrink.name: Portsmouth City Centre
foodDrink.content: Usual high street names, but has Miss Selfridge, Topshop, H&M, New Look and Primark next to one another.

foodDrink.name: Gunwharf Quays
foodDrink.content: Outlet centre, with shops like M&S, Cadburys, Claire's, Gap. Some of the prices are cheaper than the high streets, but likewise some are similar or more expensive so shopping around is a good idea.

foodDrink.name: Southsea Town Centre
foodDrink.content: A variety of small specialist shops, boutiques, art shops, delis, home furnishings. Also Knight & Lee.

foodDrink.name: Albert Road
foodDrink.content: A good bet for smaller (independent) shops, second-hand goods and antiques.

foodDrink.name: The Tenth Hole Tea Room
foodDrink.content: Great for light lunch but the highlight is the amazing home-made cakes.

foodDrink.name: abarbistro
foodDrink.content: Old Portsmouth. Modern European cuisine. Also great but you can drop a lot of money in this place, which has great service!

foodDrink.name: The Beach Club
foodDrink.content: A relatively new restaurant right on the pebbles, with the most amazing views of the Solent. Great for a cold glass of wine, stonebaked pizza and pasta.

foodDrink.name: Panero Lounge
foodDrink.content: British fare

foodDrink.name: Becketts Southsea
foodDrink.content: British-inspired cuisine

foodDrink.name: Bold Forester
foodDrink.content: Green King

foodDrink.name: The Deco
foodDrink.content: Friendly rock and alternative, sometimes metal bar.

foodDrink.name: Festing
foodDrink.content: Green King

foodDrink.name: Hole in the Wall
foodDrink.content: Small pub with a traditional feel and real ales.

foodDrink.name: The Honest Politician
foodDrink.content: A pub with pool tables and a relaxed atmosphere, and always a rocking soundtrack.

foodDrink.name: The Wine Vaults
foodDrink.content: Good cask ales and great atmosphere, arrive early if you want a seat.

foodDrink.name: Meat and Barrel
foodDrink.content: Meat majors on burgers, wings and ribs.

foodDrink.name: Croxton's Kitchen & Tap House
foodDrink.hours: T-Thu Noon-10PM, Fri Sat noon-11PM, S noon-9PM (Mon closed)
foodDrink.content: Interesting range of summery beer. Food includes: Bavett of beef, mussels.

foodDrink.name: The Lord Palmerston
foodDrink.content: Wetherspoons.

foodDrink.name: Shenanigans
foodDrink.content: Irish pub doing breakfast and occasional music.

foodDrink.name: Ship Anson
foodDrink.content: Green King overlooking the HMS Warrior.

foodDrink.name: The Old Customs House
foodDrink.content: A traditional pub in a historic building, within a modern setting. Great ales and food.

foodDrink.name: The Ship & Castle
foodDrink.content: In the ‘Devil’s Acre’ severing a carvery every day overlooking the HMS Warrior

foodDrink.name: The Chambers
foodDrink.content: A plush pub with a roof terrace.

foodDrink.name: The Dolphin
foodDrink.content: Claims to be Portsmouth's oldest pub.

foodDrink.name: Spice Island Inn
foodDrink.content: Also has amazing views of the harbour in action and a good restaurant.

foodDrink.name: The Still & West
foodDrink.content: A pub with a good view of harbour entrance and restaurant upstairs.

foodDrink.name: The Wellington
foodDrink.content: The oldest pub in Portsmouth, established in 1710.
